config.title: Children Prop

intro.title: Children Prop
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that uses the children prop to display content passed from a parent component. You will learn how to use the default slot in Vue to render child content dynamically. The main technologies involved are Vue components, slots, and template syntax. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand how to make components more reusable by allowing them to accept and display external content.
intro.usecase: The children prop is a fundamental Vue pattern for creating reusable layout components and UI containers. You'll use it when building dashboard panels that can hold any combination of charts and widgets, modal dialogs that accept custom content, or navigation menus that wrap around various link items. This approach allows you to create flexible card components, tabbed interfaces, and sidebar layouts where the parent component defines the structure while the child content remains dynamic and interchangeable.

objectives: Construct a Vue component that accepts and renders children content via slots
Apply slot syntax to pass HTML elements and text as children to components
Configure named slots to organize multiple children content sections
Manipulate slot content using scoped slots to pass data from parent to child
Initialize fallback content within slots to display when no children are provided
Integrate slot props to control how parent content interacts with child component data
Render dynamic children content by binding slot data to component state

steps.title: Import Vue and create the main component
steps.instruction: Import Vue from 'vue' and create a Vue component named App with a template section.
steps.hint: Use the standard Vue import and define a component with a template.
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and create the main App component
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Vue component named App ready to build upon.
successCriteria: Vue is imported from 'vue' and an App component with a template section is created.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported Vue from 'vue' and defined the App component with a template.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported Vue from 'vue' and created an App component with a template section.

steps.title: Create a child component to receive children
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named Card that returns a simple div element.
steps.hint: Define a component function that returns a div element. This will be the container that will later receive children content.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a Card component defined that returns a div element, ready to be enhanced with slot functionality in later steps.
successCriteria: A Card component function is created that returns an object with a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a function named Card that returns an object with a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component wasn't created correctly. You need to define a function named Card that returns an object with a template property containing a div element.

steps.title: Add initial content to the Card component
steps.instruction: Add a default slot to the Card component template by replacing the empty div with a slot element.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can use the <slot> element to create a default slot where content can be passed from parent components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component will have a default slot that can receive children content.
successCriteria: The Card component's template contains a <slot> element inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've replaced the empty div with a slot element inside the Card component's template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component still has an empty div. Try adding a <slot> element inside the div to create a default slot.

steps.title: Use the Card component in App with simple content
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, add a Card component with the text 'Hello from the Card!' between its opening and closing tags.
steps.hint: Place the Card component inside the div in the template, and write the text directly between the opening <Card> and closing </Card> tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render a Card component containing the text 'Hello from the Card!'.
successCriteria: The App component's template includes a Card component with the text 'Hello from the Card!' placed between its tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Card component is inside the div in App's template, and the text 'Hello from the Card!' is directly between the Card tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the Card component to App's template with the correct text content between its tags.

steps.title: Add multiple elements as children to Card
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's template, pass a heading element and a paragraph element as children to the Card component.
steps.hint: Place the heading and paragraph elements between the opening and closing tags of the Card component in the template.

steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component will receive multiple child elements (a heading and a paragraph) from its parent component.
successCriteria: The Card component in the App template contains both a heading element and a paragraph element as children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both a heading element and a paragraph element inside the Card component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component should contain both a heading and a paragraph element as children in the App template.

steps.title: Create a Button component with slot
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named Button that returns a <button> element with a slot inside it.
steps.hint: Define a function called Button that returns an object with a template property containing a <button> element with <slot></slot> inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a Button component that can accept dynamic content through its slot.
successCriteria: The Button component is defined as a function that returns an object with a template containing a <button> element with a <slot> inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Button component returns an object with a template property containing a <button> element with <slot></slot> inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component isn't defined correctly. It should be a function named Button that returns an object with a template containing a <button> element with a slot.

steps.title: Use Button component with different text
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, add two Button components inside the Card. Give the first Button the text 'Click Me' and the second Button the text 'Submit' as their slot content.
steps.hint: You can place multiple Button components inside the Card's template. Each Button will render its own slot content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will contain two Button instances with distinct text inside the Card, demonstrating how slot content can be customized per component instance.
successCriteria: Two Button components are added inside the Card in App's template, each with different text content (e.g., 'Click Me' and 'Submit').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly two Button components with distinct text inside the Card.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added two Button components inside the Card in the App template, each with unique text like 'Click Me' and 'Submit'.

steps.title: Add named slots to Card component
steps.instruction: In the Card component's template, add a header slot and a footer slot using the <slot> element with name attributes.
steps.hint: Use <slot name="header"></slot> for the header and <slot name="footer"></slot> for the footer. Place them inside the div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component template now has named slots for header and footer content.
successCriteria: Card component template contains <slot name="header"> and <slot name="footer"> elements inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both header and footer slots with the correct name attributes inside the Card's template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component template doesn't yet have the required named slots. Add <slot name="header"> and <slot name="footer"> inside the div.

steps.title: Use named slots in App
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, pass content to the Card's header and footer slots using template v-slot syntax.
steps.hint: Use <template v-slot:header> and <template v-slot:footer> inside the Card component tags to provide content for each named slot.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: passing content to named slots
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have template v-slot directives for both header and footer slots inside the Card component.
successCriteria: The Card component in App's template contains <template v-slot:header> and <template v-slot:footer> with content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct v-slot syntax for both header and footer.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for named slots. You need to use <template v-slot:slotName> inside the component tags.

steps.title: Combine default and named slots
steps.instruction: In the Card component's template, add the header and footer named slots around the default slot content.
steps.hint: Place <slot name="header"></slot> before the default slot, and <slot name="footer"></slot> after it, all inside the div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component template now includes slots for header, default content, and footer in a single structure.
successCriteria: Card component template contains <slot name="header"></slot>, <slot></slot>, and <slot name="footer"></slot> inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have all three slots: header (named), default, and footer (named) in the Card template.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the Card component's template. It should include slots for header, default content, and footer inside the div.
